## Definitions

- [statement] OSHA says engineering and work-practice controls should be the primary feasible means of reducing toxic chemical exposure; NIOSH describes source-capture ventilation for volatile printing-press emissions. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://www.osha.gov/chemical-hazards/ · keywords: Game print production proofing quality acceptance and safety · also: https://www.cdc.gov/niosh/engcontrols/ecd/detail37.html

## Structure and components

- [statement] CPSC’s small-parts ban covers products intended for children under three, but exempts books and other articles made of paper; entirely paper pieces detached during use-and-abuse testing are also excluded from the small-part test. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://www.cpsc.gov/FAQ/Small-Parts-and-Choking-Hazard-Labeling-FAQs · keywords: Game print production proofing quality acceptance and safety · also: https://www.cpsc.gov/Business--Manufacturing/Business-Education/Business-Guidance/Small-Parts-for-Toys-and-Childrens-Products
- [statement] CPSC permits reliance on component-supplier lead-test evidence only with due care and access to underlying test documentation, including valid testing by a CPSC-accepted laboratory. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://www.cpsc.gov/FAQ/Total-Lead-Content · keywords: Game print production proofing quality acceptance and safety
- [statement] Reliance on a component supplier’s lead test or certificate requires due care and access to underlying test documentation; a bare supplier assurance is insufficient under CPSC’s explanation. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://www.cpsc.gov/FAQ/Total-Lead-Content · keywords: Game print production proofing quality acceptance and safety
- [statement] PrintNinja describes initial custom board-game prices as budgetary and withholds a final quotation until artwork review. Treat an early estimate as provisional and ask for a written quote against the final artwork and component specification. This is its board-game quotation policy, not a universal rule for all card printers. (low confidence) — https://printninja.com/custom-board-game-pricing/ · keywords: Game print production proofing quality acceptance and safety
- [statement] Loffler describes paper and staples as excluded from its explanation of click charges. Ask what consumables, parts and maintenance a proposed service rate actually covers, and price the substrate separately unless the written agreement includes it. Do not transfer this supplier description into an assumption about every contract. (low confidence) — https://www.loffler.com/blog/true-cost-of-owning-a-commercial-printer · keywords: Game print production proofing quality acceptance and safety
- [statement] A physical sample must identify its printing process and included finishing. PrintNinja says its assembled game proof can contain digitally printed components that are not color accurate; Kuo Kau says its uncut digital sample uses actual material but excludes coating, varnish and special finishing. (high confidence) — https://printninja.com/proofing-options/ · keywords: Game print production proofing quality acceptance and safety · also: https://www.kkplayingcard.com/en/page-5998/Sample-Proof-Guide.html
- [statement] Publisher Frank West reports checking imposed PDF samples for alignment and cut lines, then counting cards and checking order, duplicates and the rulebook component list. This is a documented operator checklist, not evidence that a supplier performs these checks for the customer. (low confidence) — https://thecityofkings.com/news/requesting-samples-from-your-manufacturer/ · keywords: Game print production proofing quality acceptance and safety
- [statement] PrintNinja warns that digitally printed components within a physical game proof are not color accurate. Physical delivery alone therefore does not establish an offset-color reference for every component. (low confidence) — https://printninja.com/proofing-options/ · keywords: Game print production proofing quality acceptance and safety
- [statement] Publisher Frank West describes checking card counts, ordering and duplicates against the rulebook’s component list. This is a concrete completeness-and-collation check, separate from judging print appearance. (low confidence) — https://thecityofkings.com/news/requesting-samples-from-your-manufacturer/ · keywords: Game print production proofing quality acceptance and safety
- [statement] Kylin recommends naming and counting card faces and shared backs in a manifest; publisher Frank West independently describes counting cards and checking order, duplicates and the rulebook component list. (medium confidence) — https://m.kylinmanufactory.com/news/Board_Game_Pieces/Board_Game_Card_Stock_Guide_GSM_Core_Finish_and_Durability.html · keywords: Game print production proofing quality acceptance and safety · also: https://thecityofkings.com/news/requesting-samples-from-your-manufacturer/

## How it works

- [statement] OSHA’s printing-press roll-cleaning case rejects the minor-servicing exception when workers bypass guards and lack effective alternative protection, even when cleaning is routine, repetitive and integral to production. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://www.osha.gov/etools/lockout-tagout/case-studies/printing-press-roll-cleaning · keywords: Game print production proofing quality acceptance and safety
- [statement] MakePlayingCards’ returns page requests quality-issue contact within 3 days of arrival; its terms describe a 10-day material-and-workmanship warranty. These statements specify different windows and should be quoted separately when agreeing receipt inspection and remedies. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://www.makeplayingcards.com/guarantee.aspx · keywords: Game print production proofing quality acceptance and safety · also: https://www.makeplayingcards.com/pay_terms.aspx
- [statement] Tianyi Shengtang describes taking colour readings during production and stopping the press when readings exceed tolerance; it says batch records link finished goods to material, ink, press-run and inspection records. These are supplier-described controls. (low confidence) — https://tystprinting.com/quality/ · keywords: Game print production proofing quality acceptance and safety

## How-to and procedures

- [statement] Use the same buyer-supplied artwork for demonstrations and request the workflow through finishing. Ricoh describes start-to-finishing demonstrations, while Konica Minolta invites advance submission of the buyer’s files for printed samples. These are manufacturer offers, not independently measured results. (medium confidence) — https://www.ricoh-usa.com/en/production-printing/about/customer-experience-center · keywords: Game print production proofing quality acceptance and safety · also: https://kmbs.konicaminolta.us/client-engagement-center/
- [statement] Use representative random samples for lot decisions. NIST describes random lot selection; Minitab also recommends random selection representative of the whole lot, including stratification where needed. (high confidence) — https://www.itl.nist.gov/div898/handbook/pmc/section2/pmc21.htm · keywords: Game print production proofing quality acceptance and safety · also: https://support.minitab.com/en-us/minitab/help-and-how-to/quality-and-process-improvement/acceptance-sampling/how-to/attributes-acceptance-sampling/before-you-start/data-considerations/

## Measurements and reference values

- [statement] PrintNinja’s published defect clause treats a defect rate under 2% as a completed order. Above 2%, it may provide a proportional refund or reprint and ship replacements at its cost, with the refund/reprint choice reserved to PrintNinja. It may require defect documentation and requires reporting within 90 days of delivery. The clause does not explicitly resolve the exact 2% boundary. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://printninja.com/about/terms/ · keywords: Game print production proofing quality acceptance and safety
- [statement] PrintNinja’s terms updated July 14, 2022 treat an order with under 2% defective copies as complete; above 2% the stated remedy may be a prorated refund or replacement printing, at its discretion, with defect reports due within 90 days. The passage does not resolve the exactly-2% boundary. (low confidence) (verified as of 2022-07-14) — https://printninja.com/about/terms/ · keywords: Game print production proofing quality acceptance and safety

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] Small-parts warning requirements depend on the product and intended age, including applicable products for ages 3–6; advertising for toys subject to the warning must carry it too. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://www.cpsc.gov/Business--Manufacturing/Business-Education/Business-Guidance/CPSC-Labeling-Requirements-Overview · keywords: Game print production proofing quality acceptance and safety · also: https://www.cpsc.gov/Business--Manufacturing/Business-Education/Business-Guidance/Small-Parts-for-Toys-and-Childrens-Products
- [statement] CPSC says paper and ordinary CMYK process printing inks can avoid third-party lead testing under material determinations; this does not remove the lead-content limit or the obligation to certify compliance. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://www.cpsc.gov/FAQ/Total-Lead-Content · keywords: Game print production proofing quality acceptance and safety · also: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-16/chapter-II/subchapter-C/part-1500/section-1500.91
- [statement] The CMYK lead determination excludes spot colors, non-CMYK inks, inks outside the substrate and specified after-treatment printing; it cannot be extended automatically to every printed finish. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-04) — https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-16/chapter-II/subchapter-C/part-1500/section-1500.91 · keywords: Game print production proofing quality acceptance and safety
- [statement] CPSC identifies specific choking-warning labeling rules for products containing small parts and intended for children between three and six; that scope should be checked separately from paper exemptions to the under-three small-parts ban. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://www.cpsc.gov/Business--Manufacturing/Business-Education/Business-Guidance/CPSC-Labeling-Requirements-Overview · keywords: Game print production proofing quality acceptance and safety · also: https://www.cpsc.gov/FAQ/Small-Parts-and-Choking-Hazard-Labeling-FAQs
- [statement] CPSC says accessible children’s-product components must meet a total lead limit of 100 ppm and paint or similar surface coatings a separate 90 ppm limit. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://www.cpsc.gov/FAQ/Total-Lead-Content · keywords: Game print production proofing quality acceptance and safety
- [statement] In a DC-618 operator discussion, Andres reports that later-cut cards have more skew, while tngcas reports replacing rollers to resolve a similar problem. Use these attributed anecdotes to challenge a demo with checks across the whole sheet and run, and to ask about roller maintenance. They do not establish defects, lifetime or failure rates for other machine models. (low confidence) — https://printplanet.com/threads/duplo-dc-618-skewing-in-machine.295010/ · keywords: Game print production proofing quality acceptance and safety
- [statement] In an April 2024 PrintPlanet thread, operator COGordon reports double feeding on a Duplo 646 with lighter stock despite service-setting changes. This is a self-reported case on that model and stock class, not a measured failure rate or proof of a defect in another machine model. Use it to justify observing real-stock feeding during the demo. (low confidence) — https://printplanet.com/threads/methods-for-reducing-static-on-duplo-646.294079/ · keywords: Game print production proofing quality acceptance and safety
- [statement] PrintNinja cautions that a single domestic digital-offset unit cannot be treated as a one-to-one comparison with its offset product because materials, finishes and binding techniques differ. (low confidence) — https://printninja.com/electronic-proofing-steps/ · keywords: Game print production proofing quality acceptance and safety
- [statement] MakePlayingCards tells customers to verify design and order details before submitting: its automated production policy says cancellations and changes cannot be made after submission. - [statement] MakePlayingCards asks customers to report quality issues within 3 days of arrival. Personalized products qualify for return only for a manufacturing error or product defect. A granted remedy can be replacement, refund or account credit after returned items are inspected; the customer is responsible for returning products unused and undamaged. Its separate terms require written supplier agreement to modified terms, so a buyer should obtain agreement to project-specific acceptance changes before submitting the order. That publisher’s service threshold is not evidence that every game should accept the same dimensional error. ## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] OSHA requires guarding where operation exposes employees to injury and lists guillotine cutters; the guard must prevent access to the danger zone during the operating cycle, rather than merely warn. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://www.osha.gov/laws-regs/regulations/standardnumber/1910/1910.212 · keywords: Game print production proofing quality acceptance and safety · also: https://www.osha.gov/laws-regs/standardinterpretations/2004-04-07
- [statement] UK HSE identifies failure to refit guards as a major cause of printing-industry accidents. This supports guard-restoration checks as an operational concern, rather than establishing a US legal requirement. (low confidence) — https://www.hse.gov.uk/printing/faqs.htm · keywords: Game print production proofing quality acceptance and safety
- [statement] OSHA lists guillotine cutters among machines usually requiring point-of-operation guarding; hand tools for placing or removing material supplement rather than replace required guards. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://www.osha.gov/etools/machine-guarding/introduction/general-requirements · keywords: Game print production proofing quality acceptance and safety
- [statement] Duplo says application testing produces an emailed report. Request that report and returned sample output as documentary evidence rather than accepting a verbal compatibility assurance. (low confidence) — https://app.duplousa.com/contact/atr.aspx · keywords: Game print production proofing quality acceptance and safety
- [statement] PrintNinja labels one published price configuration as a 54-card poker deck with a printed tuck box. Use that example only for that configuration; obtain a separate quote for the commissioned game instead of scaling an unrelated deck price. (low confidence) — https://printninja.com/printing-prices/card-game-printing/ · keywords: Game print production proofing quality acceptance and safety
- [statement] Duplo’s application-testing form says laminated substrates require compatibility testing and promises an emailed results report. Request qualification of the intended finished stock rather than assuming that an accepted paper weight establishes compatibility. (low confidence) — https://app.duplousa.com/contact/atr.aspx · keywords: Game print production proofing quality acceptance and safety
- [statement] For an equipment quote, request a full-system cost schedule rather than relying on the press price or a demonstration calculator alone. Printing Impressions reports that finishing and landed delivery belong in ownership analysis; Konica Minolta describes its demonstration cost review as raw-cost calculators. This is a procurement recommendation, not a measured cost or break-even estimate. (medium confidence) — https://www.piworld.com/article/anatomy-determining-total-cost-ownership-production-inkjet-presses/ · keywords: Game print production proofing quality acceptance and safety · also: https://kmbs.konicaminolta.us/client-engagement-center/
- [statement] Panda describes separate approval gates: approved digital proofs precede sampling; approval of the pre-production copy and component samples starts mass production; review and approval of the mass-production copy precedes assembly of the remaining games. Its mass-production copy arrives when production is nearly complete, so this is an assembly checkpoint rather than a promise that printing has not begun. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://pandagm.com/our-process/ · keywords: Game print production proofing quality acceptance and safety
- [statement] PrintNinja publishes differently scoped color statements: its general board-game explainer calls CMYK hard proofs accurate, but its component-specific proof specification excludes digital components from color accuracy and its terms disclaim guaranteed matching without ordered spot/Pantone color. Attribute these positions and obtain component-specific acceptance terms rather than treating the general statement as a universal guarantee. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://printninja.com/custom-board-games/board-game-prototyping-and-proofing/ · keywords: Game print production proofing quality acceptance and safety · also: https://printninja.com/proofing-options/, https://printninja.com/about/terms/
- [statement] PrintNinja describes soft proofs as layout references rather than reliable previews of printed color. Its electronic-proofing guide explicitly says the screen proof does not establish final colors. (high confidence) — https://printninja.com/about/terms/ · keywords: Game print production proofing quality acceptance and safety · also: https://printninja.com/electronic-proofing-steps/
- [statement] Kylin recommends recording conditional approval in a numbered, revision-controlled report, with both parties retaining its signed or acknowledged final version. This supplies a concrete written revision record rather than an ambiguous approval email. (low confidence) — https://www.kylinmanufactory.com/news/Designing_A_Board_Game/Board_Game_Preproduction_Sample_Approval_Guide.html · keywords: Game print production proofing quality acceptance and safety
- [statement] Kylin describes a golden sample as an approved, controlled physical reference retained for production, used alongside written tolerances rather than replacing them. This is manufacturer guidance, not an independently measured quality result. (low confidence) — https://www.kylinmanufactory.com/news/Designing_A_Board_Game/Board_Game_Preproduction_Sample_Approval_Guide.html · keywords: Game print production proofing quality acceptance and safety
- [statement] Acceptance sampling is primarily for deciding whether a lot is likely acceptable, rather than estimating its quality. NIST distinguishes this immediate lot decision from long-run quality control, while QIMA describes AQL as risk management. A passed sample therefore must not be presented as a measured defect rate for the entire shipment. (medium confidence) — https://www.itl.nist.gov/div898/handbook/pmc/section2/pmc21.htm · keywords: Game print production proofing quality acceptance and safety · also: https://www.qima.com/aql-acceptable-quality-limit
- [statement] QIMA describes reinspection after corrections are completed to check the batch against the agreed AQL before shipment. This supports a correction-and-verification step rather than treating the first inspection report as final closure. (low confidence) — https://www.qima.com/aql-acceptable-quality-limit · keywords: Game print production proofing quality acceptance and safety
- [statement] Minitab recommends agreeing both AQL and RQL with the supplier; its guidance describes acceptance and rejection probabilistically rather than as certainty. (low confidence) — https://support.minitab.com/en-us/minitab/help-and-how-to/quality-and-process-improvement/acceptance-sampling/how-to/attributes-acceptance-sampling/before-you-start/data-considerations/ · keywords: Game print production proofing quality acceptance and safety
- [statement] Kylin recommends new approval after a mill or stock change, rather than accepting a similar marketing name. (low confidence) — https://m.kylinmanufactory.com/news/Board_Game_Pieces/Board_Game_Card_Stock_Guide_GSM_Core_Finish_and_Durability.html · keywords: Game print production proofing quality acceptance and safety

## Facts and statements

- [statement] CPSC classifies a children’s product by primary intended use for children aged 12 or younger, considering reasonable manufacturer statements, marketing, consumer recognition and age-determination guidance; an age label alone does not control classification. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://www.cpsc.gov/FAQ/Childrens-Products · keywords: Game print production proofing quality acceptance and safety
- [statement] CPSC treats traditional playing cards and similar games appealing to a general audience as general-use products; child-oriented features or junior packaging can change that classification. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://www.cpsc.gov/FAQ/Childrens-Products · keywords: Game print production proofing quality acceptance and safety
- [statement] For toys primarily intended for children aged 12 or younger, CPSC requires applicable third-party testing by an accepted laboratory and a Children’s Product Certificate; the manufacturer or importer must identify applicable toy-standard sections. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://www.cpsc.gov/FAQ/Toy-Safety · keywords: Game print production proofing quality acceptance and safety · also: https://www.cpsc.gov/FAQ/Childrens-Products
- [statement] CPSC distinguishes ASTM F963’s under-14 toy scope from the federal third-party-testing threshold for products intended primarily for children 12 or younger. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://www.cpsc.gov/FAQ/Toy-Safety · keywords: Game print production proofing quality acceptance and safety
- [statement] CPSC exempts labeling, instructions and producer markings from third-party laboratory testing, while requiring CPC certification of all applicable toy-standard sections. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://www.cpsc.gov/FAQ/Toy-Safety · keywords: Game print production proofing quality acceptance and safety
- [statement] Children’s products need permanent tracking information on product and packaging to the extent practicable, including the responsible firm, production date and location, and identifying production information such as a batch or run number. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://www.cpsc.gov/FAQ/Tracking-Label · keywords: Game print production proofing quality acceptance and safety · also: https://www.cpsc.gov/Business--Manufacturing/Business-Education/Business-Guidance/CPSC-Labeling-Requirements-Overview, https://www.cpsc.gov/FAQ/Toy-Safety
- [statement] CPSC distinguishes a toy’s substantive flammability obligations from premarket testing: the FHSA prohibits hazardous flammable children’s toys even though this requirement does not mandate premarket or third-party testing. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://www.cpsc.gov/FAQ/Toy-Safety · keywords: Game print production proofing quality acceptance and safety
- [statement] OSHA’s printing interpretation limits the minor-servicing exception to routine, repetitive, integral production work with effective alternative protection. Normal guillotine blade changing requires an energy-control procedure with lockout/tagout and any necessary guarding. (low confidence) (verified as of 2004-04-07) — https://www.osha.gov/laws-regs/standardinterpretations/2004-04-07 · keywords: Game print production proofing quality acceptance and safety
- [statement] The MBM-hosted manual describes a movable guard and two-hand control as cutting safeguards for IDEAL 6655. (low confidence) — https://mbmcorp.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/TRIUMPH-6655-op-manual-1399.pdf · keywords: Game print production proofing quality acceptance and safety
- [statement] Where OSHA’s Hazard Communication standard applies, employers need a written program for chemical labels, SDSs and training; SDSs must be immediately accessible, and training covers initial assignment and new chemical hazards. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://www.osha.gov/laws-regs/regulations/standardnumber/1910/1910.1200 · keywords: Game print production proofing quality acceptance and safety
- [statement] NIOSH identifies inhalation and skin-contact hazards during press cleaning. Its printing LEV example reports vapor and dust measurement reductions of 83 percent and 67 percent; these are case results, not workshop performance predictions. (low confidence) — https://www.cdc.gov/niosh/engcontrols/ecd/detail37.html · keywords: Game print production proofing quality acceptance and safety
- [statement] A NIOSH educational vignette links visual symptoms to an amine-containing additive used with water-based ink. NIOSH calls the story loosely based on evaluations and cautions that its facility-specific recommendations may not generalize. (low confidence) — https://www.cdc.gov/niosh/bulletin/2015/medical-mystery1b.html · keywords: Game print production proofing quality acceptance and safety
- [statement] OSHA’s lithography guidance identifies repeated reaching, pinching, prolonged standing and low-table bending in hand collation; it recommends reachable stacks, adjusted work height, posture variation and reduced exposure time. (low confidence) — https://www.osha.gov/etools/printing-industry/lithography · keywords: Game print production proofing quality acceptance and safety
- [statement] CPSC’s labeling overview still names ASTM F963-17, whereas its Toy Safety FAQ names ASTM F963-23 with an April 20, 2024 effective date. This is a mismatch between the two cited pages, not evidence that both editions currently govern. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://www.cpsc.gov/Business--Manufacturing/Business-Education/Business-Guidance/CPSC-Labeling-Requirements-Overview · keywords: Game print production proofing quality acceptance and safety · also: https://www.cpsc.gov/FAQ/Toy-Safety

- [statement] NIOSH identifies press-cleaning solvent vapors and skin absorption as printing hazards; its control guidance describes local exhaust that captures vapor near the press and exhausts it outside with replacement air. - [statement] For employers using hazardous workplace chemicals, OSHA requires labels, safety data sheets and worker training about hazards and protective measures. - [statement] OSHA’s lithography guidance identifies repetitive forceful paper gripping, awkward wrist postures and bending in finishing work; suggested controls include smaller handled stacks, neutral hand postures and adjustable work surfaces. - [statement] A production-equipment discussion recommends checking whether click charges vary by sheet size and remain fixed for the lease term; another print-shop operator recommends checking minimum-usage fees. (low confidence) — https://printplanet.com/threads/new-owner-new-equipment.292427/ · keywords: Game print production proofing quality acceptance and safety
- [statement] Duplo publishes a maximum DC-648 speed of 40 sheets per minute. This is a manufacturer sheet-processing rating, not demonstrated finished-game output. Protocol recommendation: time the whole sample workflow, including setup and downtime, and count completed decks; Ricoh offers workflow demonstrations and Loffler identifies setup and downtime as costs. (medium confidence) — https://www.duplousa.com/product/dc-648-slitter-cutter-creaser/ · keywords: Game print production proofing quality acceptance and safety · also: https://www.ricoh-usa.com/en/production-printing/about/customer-experience-center, https://www.loffler.com/blog/true-cost-of-owning-a-commercial-printer
- [statement] Duplo’s DC-648 page identifies a separately sold PC Controller. Ask the written equipment quote to name the supplied controller configuration and price any required computer explicitly. (low confidence) — https://www.duplousa.com/product/dc-648-slitter-cutter-creaser/ · keywords: Game print production proofing quality acceptance and safety
- [statement] Printing Impressions advises checking warranty and service exclusions, separate software/DFE contracts and upgrade costs before closing. Recommended quote protocol: require these coverage boundaries and recurring charges in writing. The article is historical industry reporting, not a current vendor service offer. (low confidence) — https://www.piworld.com/article/anatomy-determining-total-cost-ownership-production-inkjet-presses/ · keywords: Game print production proofing quality acceptance and safety
- [statement] Freeze card count, material, finish and packaging in the request for quote. PrintNinja’s guide explicitly asks about those specifications, and its public price examples identify a particular deck and box configuration. Treat the commissioned game configuration as a separate custom request; do not reuse an example-deck price as its quote. (medium confidence) — https://printninja.com/game-quote-guide/ · keywords: Game print production proofing quality acceptance and safety · also: https://printninja.com/printing-prices/card-game-printing/
- [statement] Recommended comparison protocol: send one unchanged job specification and identical artwork to each candidate; request returned samples and a written account of the tested stock and workflow. The basis is the vendors’ own-file demonstrations and substrate qualification, not evidence that these suppliers have already produced this game successfully. (medium confidence) — https://kmbs.konicaminolta.us/client-engagement-center/ · keywords: Game print production proofing quality acceptance and safety · also: https://app.duplousa.com/contact/atr.aspx
- [statement] Electronic proofs serve content and layout review, not physical stock or reliable printed-color acceptance: PrintNinja describes PDF layout/trim/fold review and disclaims accurate color; Kuo Kau explicitly excludes physical materials and actual print-color reference from its artwork e-proof. (high confidence) — https://printninja.com/about/terms/ · keywords: Game print production proofing quality acceptance and safety · also: https://www.kkplayingcard.com/en/page-5998/Sample-Proof-Guide.html
- [statement] Kuo Kau distinguishes an offset pre-production sample made on the intended mass-production press and materials from a mass-production sample randomly selected from the completed run; the former targets the closest color match, while the latter checks actual production. (low confidence) — https://www.kkplayingcard.com/en/page-5998/Sample-Proof-Guide.html · keywords: Game print production proofing quality acceptance and safety
- [statement] Frank West uses blank, cut and packaged white samples to evaluate material, dimensions and box fit separately from printed content. His production sample is a manually assembled copy reviewed before the rest are assembled and packed; he warns that correcting errors then may require paying for reprinting or changes. (low confidence) — https://thecityofkings.com/news/requesting-samples-from-your-manufacturer/ · keywords: Game print production proofing quality acceptance and safety
- [statement] PrintNinja requires a submitted and accepted written change order for changes after quotation acceptance and does not guarantee verbal change requests. Its proof terms also say approval can be a button click, written approval or verbal approval, and later changes may incur fees; therefore a revision request must not be confused with an accepted production change. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://printninja.com/about/terms/ · keywords: Game print production proofing quality acceptance and safety
- [statement] A publisher operator account describes a mass-production copy as the final publisher quality check before assembly and reports replacing Nut Hunt dice after reviewing that copy. This is a reported experience, not a measured defect rate. (low confidence) — https://www.reddit.com/r/boardgames/comments/136kvuo · keywords: Game print production proofing quality acceptance and safety
- [statement] PrintNinja excludes typos and other content errors from its guarantee and says its prepress review does not check those issues. The buyer must finish content review before approving production. (low confidence) — https://printninja.com/pledge/ · keywords: Game print production proofing quality acceptance and safety
- [statement] For reprints, Kylin recommends comparing the new lot against the retained sample and prior data, and confirming that artwork, materials, tools and subcontractors have not changed. (low confidence) — https://www.kylinmanufactory.com/news/Safety_Tests_for_Games/Board_Game_Quality_Control_The_Publisher_s_Inspection_Checklist.html · keywords: Game print production proofing quality acceptance and safety
- [statement] Honray’s published defect scheme treats defects that make a game unusable, incomplete or unsellable as major, and cosmetic imperfections without gameplay impact as minor. These are its published categories, not a universal project-specific acceptance agreement. (low confidence) — https://www.honraygames.com/quality-control/ · keywords: Game print production proofing quality acceptance and safety
- [statement] In its January 5, 2023 Turing Machine incident notice, Hachette relayed Scorpion Masqué’s report of missing or damaged inserts and stated that files for future prints had been reviewed with the factory to correct the insert issue. This is an attributed corrective-action account, not proof of an achieved defect rate. (low confidence) — https://www.hachetteboardgames.com/blogs/infos/turing-machine-1st-printing-issues · keywords: Game print production proofing quality acceptance and safety
- [statement] PRINTING United Alliance describes system certification around a defined configuration that includes the engine, DFE, software and applicable materials, and requires recertification after major hardware or software upgrades. Certification evidence should therefore be checked against the configuration actually used. (low confidence) — https://idealliance.org/systems-certification/g7-press-control-system-certification/ · keywords: Game print production proofing quality acceptance and safety
- [statement] Retain a coded approved physical reference for repeat orders. Kylin recommends retaining the chosen sample and its purchase-specification code; Tianyi Shengtang says it logs approved samples against production batches. (medium confidence) — https://m.kylinmanufactory.com/news/Board_Game_Pieces/Board_Game_Card_Stock_Guide_GSM_Core_Finish_and_Durability.html · keywords: Game print production proofing quality acceptance and safety · also: https://tystprinting.com/quality/
- [statement] Kylin recommends defining allowable cutting, registration, colour and finishing variation separately from functional defects, and using manifests, sorting, weight checks and random full-deck verification for count and collation. This is manufacturer guidance, not an independently measured yield. (low confidence) — https://m.kylinmanufactory.com/news/Board_Game_Pieces/Board_Game_Card_Stock_Guide_GSM_Core_Finish_and_Durability.html · keywords: Game print production proofing quality acceptance and safety
- [statement] Protect retained reference samples from environmental change. Kylin recommends flat archive storage away from sunlight, heat and handling; RIT explains that heat, light and pollutants can fade prints or shift their colour. (medium confidence) — https://m.kylinmanufactory.com/news/Board_Game_Pieces/Board_Game_Card_Stock_Guide_GSM_Core_Finish_and_Durability.html · keywords: Game print production proofing quality acceptance and safety · also: https://www.rit.edu/ipi/dp3/fade
